questions.question: Solve 3x − 4 = 20 formally, naming the inverse used at each step.
questions.expected_answer: Add 4 (the additive inverse of −4) to both sides: 3x = 24. Multiply both sides by 1/3 (the multiplicative inverse of 3), i.e. divide by 3: x = 8. Check: 3(8) − 4 = 20.

questions.question: Why does x² = 49 have two solutions while x³ = −8 has one?
questions.expected_answer: Squaring loses the sign: 7² and (−7)² are both 49, so both are solutions. Cubing keeps the sign: only (−2)³ = −8, so the cube root gives one answer.

questions.question: How are the laws of exponents used to solve 2^x × 2³ = 2⁷?
questions.expected_answer: The multiplication law gives 2^(x+3) on the left. Equal powers of the same base have equal exponents, so x + 3 = 7 and x = 4. Check: 2⁴ × 2³ = 16 × 8 = 128 = 2⁷.
